questions.q: Why is Spark's Python API significant for this course?
options: PySpark IS Python — you're not learning a separate Spark-specific language, you're using Python itself to control Spark
Spark has no Python API at all
PySpark is a completely different language unrelated to Python
PySpark only works with Java, not Python
questions.explain: Every DataFrame operation in the PySpark chapter is genuine Python code calling into Spark's engine.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four places Python shows up in real data engineering work, per this lesson?
options: Talking to APIs
ETL scripts
Designing user interface mockups
Orchestration glue code
questions.explain: The four named uses are ETL scripts, APIs, orchestration glue code, and PySpark itself — UI design isn't one of them.

questions.q: What is this chapter's scope, according to the lesson?
options: A complete computer science degree condensed into 15 lessons
Exactly the Python a data engineer actually uses — not a general 'learn to program' course, and not professional software engineering topics like classes or testing frameworks
Exclusively how to build user interfaces in Python
Only Python syntax with no practical application
questions.explain: The chapter is deliberately scoped to get students fluent enough for the Spark and PySpark chapters that follow.

options: Python's package installer, used to get libraries like pandas and requests onto your machine
A type of Python variable
A Spark-specific command
A code editor
questions.explain: pip is how Lessons 21 and 23's pandas and requests libraries actually get installed.

questions.q: What does Lesson 27 build, tying this chapter's lessons together?
options: A small, real ETL script that reads, filters, and writes data, combining everything from Lessons 13-26
A Spark cluster from scratch
A REST API server
A full production-grade data warehouse
questions.explain: Lesson 27 is the chapter's capstone, previewing the exact pattern shown in this lesson's code sample.
